newsitem.title: GREECE: PRESS DIGEST - GREEK GENERAL NEWS - DEC 20.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - GREEK GENERAL NEWS - DEC 20.

text.p: Leading stories in the Greek general press:

--Prime Minister Costas Simitis maintained his tough stance on the farmers' demands to the end yesterday, refusing to meet with representatives of the approximately 5,000 who had descended on Athens to protest. The farmers returned to their blockades last night vowing to carry on till the end but it appears the barricades are unravelling.
--Conservative opposition leader Miltiades Evert locked horns with Simitis over the farmers at the budget debate in Parliament in what was a fierce and at times personal attack.
--Lady Luck now has bedtimes: a new draft bill will define opening and closing times for casinos, putting an end to all-night vigils at blackjack.
--The farmers' protest in Athens yesterday was peaceful and fruitless: farmers will decide today whether they will be spending Christmas on the barricades.

--The Peru hostage drama: The Greek foreign ministry has reportedly ordered Greece's ambassador to Peru to leave as soon as he is released from captivity. But the rebels released Alkiviadis Karokis on condition he negotiate for the release of the hostages.
--Journalist Elly Stai has been charged with perjury in her testimony to a parliament fact-finding commission on the award of a casino contract. The commission now wants access to her bank accounts.
--The government's new offensive on the market is calculated to increase competitiveness and bring inflation down to below the 5.0 percent mark.
--Ports are closed for another 24 hours as roads remain blocked. The impasse at yesterday's farmers' protest bodes ill for those wanting to travel ahead of Christmas.
